guide.description: tr <from> <to> translates characters one-for-one: every character in <from> gets swapped for the character at the same position in <to>. Unlike every other tool in this course, tr only ever reads stdin — it has no file argument — so it always sits on the right side of a pipe. With -d it drops every character in its argument instead of replacing anything.

flags.desc: delete every occurrence of these characters instead of translating

exercises.title: Translate one character
exercises.task: Pipe access.log through tr to replace every lowercase 'o' with the digit '0'.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: tr only reads stdin, so it has to come after a pipe: cat <file> | tr <from> <to>
The character to replace is a lowercase o, swapped for the digit 0

check.expected:
200 GET /h0me
404 GET /missing
200 GET /ab0ut
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /h0me
404 GET /0ld-page

exercises.expectedOutput:
200 GET /h0me
404 GET /missing
200 GET /ab0ut
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /h0me
404 GET /0ld-page
